title: User API errors during morning peak
executive_summary: INC-009 (SEV2) covers elevated 5xx errors on user endpoints affecting api-gateway and user-service, starting 2026-09-26 at 08:00Z. The investigation status is ROOT_CAUSE_IDENTIFIED. The leading hypothesis (H1, confidence 0.63) is a deployment regression: the user-service 7.1.3 to 7.2.0 deployment (dep-c02e51b7, 07:56Z, switch ORM to batch loader) introduced a failure in the ProfileBatchLoader path. Logs show NullPointerException in ProfileBatchLoader.load under v7.2.0 (log-47ccff14, logpat-user-service-2347725d). user-service error rate rose from a 0.41% baseline to a 15.64% window mean (max 26.11%) with onset at 07:57Z, and p95 latency rose from 79 ms to 374 ms. api-gateway error rate rose from 0.47% to about 7.8% with flat gateway latency, consistent with propagation of upstream 500s (logpat-api-gateway-c1d874f7). Request rate, DB connection utilisation, and CPU stayed flat, which argues against capacity saturation. The critic approved the finding. This is the most probable explanation, not a confirmed fact: the per-endpoint breakdown and the code diff were not reviewed.

hypotheses.description: The user-service 7.2.0 deployment (dep-c02e51b7, ORM switched to batch loader) introduced a regression in the ProfileBatchLoader path that causes a substantial share of GET /v1/users requests to fail with 500s; api-gateway surfaces these as its own 5xx rate. Mechanism: Deploy 7.1.3->7.2.0 at 07:56Z -> ProfileBatchLoader.load raises NullPointerException on some requests -> user-service returns 500 (error_rate ~15-25%, p95 latency up due to failing/retried work) -> api-gateway receives 500s from user-service and its error_rate rises to ~6-8% with flat gateway latency. Flat request rate, DB connection utilisation, CPU, memory, and timeouts argue against capacity saturation and point to an application-level fault.

critic_review.summary: H1 (user-service 7.2.0 regression) is the leading hypothesis and is well supported. The deploy at 07:56Z precedes the onset at 07:57Z. User-service error rate steps from 0.41% to 22.8% between the 07:55 and 08:00 samples, and p95 latency rises from 72ms to 669ms with the same onset. Request rate is flat (+1%), and DB connections, CPU and memory are flat. Round-2 re-query confirms api-gateway error rate follows the same onset (0.47% to 7.8%) with flat gateway p95, which matches propagation of upstream 500s. No configuration changes occurred in the window. The only in-scope change is the deploy, and the NPE signature names that new code path. H3 is rejected as a cause: a telemetry problem cannot produce real 500s and the metrics series are complete. H2 is weakly supported, with no competing change found and no unmeasured fault that would explain the step at the deploy time.

assessments.reasoning: Deploy 07:56Z precedes the tool-detected onset 07:57Z. User-service error and p95 step at the same time. Gateway 5xx rate follows with flat gateway latency, consistent with propagation. Flat load, DB, CPU and memory argue against saturation. No config changes in the window. The NPE count is low relative to the error rate, but the logs are PARTIAL_DATA on every query, so the gap is attributable to log incompleteness rather than a contradiction. The 7.2.0 diff was not verified and is a limitation, not a blocker.

No competing in-scope change exists: config change query returned none, and no feature-flag log was found. The step aligns with the deploy and the error signature is in the new code path. Remaining unmeasured-fault possibility is speculative.

Telemetry degradation cannot produce 500s or the latency and error step seen on two services. Metric series have zero missing points. Partial logs explain only the count gap, not the cause. Not a root-cause category for this incident.

root_cause_statement: ROOT CAUSE IDENTIFIED (critic-approved; still an INFERENCE from evidence): deployment_regression in user-service - The user-service 7.2.0 deployment (dep-c02e51b7, ORM switched to batch loader) introduced a regression in the ProfileBatchLoader path that causes a substantial share of GET /v1/users requests to fail with 500s; api-gateway surfaces these as its own 5xx rate.
corrective_actions: Roll back user-service from 7.2.0 to 7.1.3 (dep-c02e51b7 reversal) to stop the 500s, then confirm that user-service and api-gateway error rates return to baseline (~0.4%).
Until rollback completes, reduce load on the failing path if a feature flag or routing option for the batch loader exists.
Re-check api-gateway 5xx and user-service p95 latency for 15 minutes after rollback to verify recovery and close the incident.
preventive_actions: Review the 7.2.0 diff for ProfileBatchLoader.load and add null handling for missing profile or batch-key inputs, with a regression test that covers that input.
Add pre-production or canary testing for ORM and data-access changes, and gate promotion on error rate and p95 latency comparisons against the 7.1.3 baseline.
Ensure that logging covers all user-service request paths so that the failing share of GET /v1/users requests can be measured per endpoint.
monitoring_recommendations: Alert when user-service error_rate exceeds 2% for 5 minutes, and when api-gateway 5xx rate exceeds 1% for the user routes.
